chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 03 (Unit 13: Biochemistry & Macromolecules)
subject: chemistry-10

questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is present in DNA but absent in RNA?
questions.explanation: Thymine ($T$) is exclusive to DNA; in RNA, uracil ($U$) replaces thymine.

questions.question: Proteins are biopolymers formed by amino acids linked together through:
questions.explanation: Amino acids condense via peptide bonds formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another.

questions.question: Which fat-soluble vitamin is vital for calcium absorption in bones and prevents rickets?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D regulates calcium and phosphate metabolism; deficiency leads to rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) results in which clinical disease?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C deficiency, leading to impaired collagen synthesis, bleeding gums, and petechiae.

questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrates is classified as a disaccharide?
questions.explanation: Sucrose ($C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}$) is a disaccharide composed of one glucose unit and one fructose unit.

questions.question: Which polysaccharide is the primary structural component of plant cell walls and makes up 95% of cotton?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is an unbranched polymer of glucose providing structural rigidity to plant cell walls.

questions.question: What is the primary biological function of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)?

options.A: Storage and transmission of genetic hereditary information

questions.explanation: DNA contains the genetic blueprint that directs protein synthesis and passes hereditary instructions across generations.

questions.question: Fats and oils are chemically defined as triglycerides, which are esters of fatty acids with:
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are triesters formed from one molecule of the triol glycerol and three fatty acid chains.

questions.question: How many standard amino acids are utilized by living systems to synthesize proteins?
questions.explanation: There are 20 standard $\alpha$-amino acids encoded by DNA that assemble into biological proteins.

questions.question: Which carbohydrate gives a characteristic blue-black complex with iodine solution?
questions.explanation: Helical amylose coils in starch entrap iodine molecules, forming an intense blue-black diagnostic complex.

questions.question: Subcutaneous adipose fat tissue in mammals acts primarily as:

options.A: A thermal insulator against heat loss

questions.explanation: Fat layers beneath mammalian skin have low thermal conductivity, conserving internal body heat.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an unsaturated fatty acid found in olive oil?
questions.explanation: Oleic acid contains a double bond in its 18-carbon chain, making it an unsaturated fatty acid.
